items.passage: Transcript: Hello, this is Lucian Moreau-Park at the International Student Office, with two things for anyone travelling over the winter break. First, travel signatures. Normally you leave your enrolment letter at our front desk and pick it up three working days later. This month two of our advisers are away, so undergraduate letters will take six working days. Graduate letters go through the graduate school this term instead, and those are taking four. Enrolment letters themselves still come from the registrar in one working day, so request yours early. Second, the winter travel briefing. We'd planned it for Wednesday at eleven in Room 329, but that clashes with a chemistry exam, so it's moving. It'll now be on Thursday at noon, upstairs in Room 433. The slides will be posted afterwards, but the question time won't be recorded.
items.prompt: [Announcement — International student office] How long will a travel signature take for an undergraduate this month?
items.explanation: The speaker says "undergraduate letters will take six working days." "Three working days" is the usual turnaround ("pick it up three working days later"), which does not apply this month. "Four working days" is the time for graduate letters, which "go through the graduate school ... and those are taking four." "One working day" is how long the registrar takes to issue an enrolment letter, not the signature.
